answer: Each agent posts a signed quill of its identity to a distributed ledger anchored at the jetty of the network’s consensus layer, then locks an ember‑sized bond that can be slashed. When a newcomer challenges an identity, peers run a deterministic proof that any duplicate signatures would expose overlapping nonce ranges, automatically triggering a slash of the bond and revoking the colliding IDs. Because the bond must equal the computational cost of forging a unique cryptographic proof, an attacker must expend real tokens for every fake node, making a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
